'''Roman Schnabel''' (June 11, 1968) is a physics professor at the [[University of Hamburg]]. He specializes in [[gravitational wave detection]] and [[quantum optics]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schnabel |first1=Roman |last2=Korobko |first2=Mikhail |title=Optical sensitivities of current gravitational wave observatories at higher kHz, MHz and GHz frequencies |journal=Scientific Reports |volume=15 |pages=25733 |year=2025 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-08668-x  |doi-access=free|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-08668-x |access-date=28 February 2026|publisher = Nature Communications|pmc=12267846 }}</ref>

He has made contributions to the field, including the detection of gravitational waves from binary black hole mergers. He received the Special [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] as a member of the [[LIGO]] team.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Advanced LIGO detector performance in the fourth observing run |journal=Physical Review D |volume=111 |issue=6 |article-number=062002 |year=2025 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.111.062002 |url=https://journals.aps.org/prd/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevD.111.062002 |access-date=28 February 2026|hdl=1871.1/6d56a0e4-4845-47bd-a085-c35e6a757c3f |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
